reflection: Across rounds, factors help in 2023 and 2025 but hurt in 2024 (and often 2022), mostly via Random Forest. Volume-based factors (nvda_volume_surge_lead, qqq_volume_surge_peer) and smoothed close location are the best, but their sign appears regime dependent. Pairs add roughly the sum of their parts, so no real synergy yet. I will try to make volume factors regime-robust (e.g. relative to volatility, rank-like via zscore, log ratios to reduce skew) and test new ideas like intraday-vs-overnight decomposition, down-volume asymmetry, and peer range/volatility.

lessons.name: qqq_volume_surge_signed_5d
lessons.lesson: Signing the QQQ volume surge by one-day direction duplicated QQQ_return_1d information and removed the unsigned stress signal, so it lost the 2025 gain.

lessons.name: aapl_close_loc_10d_centered
lessons.lesson: A 10-day window averages away the short-term close-location signal, so the effect vanished in most years.

lessons.name: aapl_high_low_reversal_5d
lessons.lesson: It is a stochastic-style position largely duplicating close_to_ma20 (0.84), giving no new directional information.

lessons.name: aapl_volume_price_pressure
lessons.lesson: Signed volume surge was close to zero overall and flipped between years, as the volume signal only matters in turbulent regimes and the sign multiplier added noise.

lessons.name: nvda_volume_surge_lead
lessons.lesson: Apple's volume relative to NVDA's helped RF in 2023 and 2025 but not 2022 and 2024, suggesting a nonlinear regime-dependent signal that is skewed by volume spikes.

lessons.name: qqq_trend_vs_aapl_trend_20d
lessons.lesson: It overlaps with AAPL 20d momentum (0.58) and only helped RF in 2023 and 2025, too small to separate from noise.

factors.name: log_aapl_nvda_volume_ratio_z20
factors.hypothesis: The raw volume surge difference is dominated by spikes and regime scale; a log ratio z-scored over 20 days is scale-free and less skewed, which should stabilise the 2022/2024 failures.

factors.name: aapl_close_loc_3d_mean
factors.hypothesis: The 5d mean helped in 2023/2025 but 10d lost the signal; a shorter 3d window may catch sharper short-term buying/selling pressure and reduce overlap with 5d return.

factors.name: aapl_intraday_minus_overnight_5d
factors.hypothesis: Splitting returns into intraday versus overnight over 5 days captures who controls the move (retail/day vs institutional/overnight), distinct from close-to-close returns.

factors.name: nvda_range_vs_aapl_range
factors.formula: subtract(safe_divide(subtract(NVDA_High, NVDA_Low), NVDA_Close), multiply(safe_divide(subtract(AAPL_High, AAPL_Low), AAPL_Close), 2))
factors.hypothesis: Tech risk appetite shows up in NVDA's intraday range relative to Apple's; when NVDA ranges widen much more than Apple's, Apple may catch up or rebound next day.

factors.name: qqq_range_expansion_vs_aapl_volume
factors.hypothesis: Volume surge relative to NVDA may matter only when the market is in range expansion; QQQ range relative to its 20d average describes that condition and complements the volume factor.

factors.name: aapl_msft_volume_gap_signed_close_loc
factors.formula: subtract(rolling_mean(safe_divide(subtract(MSFT_Close, MSFT_Low), subtract(MSFT_High, MSFT_Low)), 5), rolling_mean(safe_divide(subtract(NVDA_Close, NVDA_Low), subtract(NVDA_High, NVDA_Low)), 5))
factors.hypothesis: Apple's smoothed close location may work better when conditioned on peers' buying pressure; MSFT minus NVDA 5d close location describes peer-lead strength differing from Apple's own.
